To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 3D-quantitative structure-activity relationship analysis of the imadizoles as dual ETA/AT1 receptor antagonists was performed and five compounds were identified to be the potential dual antagonists against ETA and AT1 receptors.

the 3D QSAR model of the imidazoles compounds is generated from the conformer obtained by QPLD and it is used to reveal the details of structure-activity relationship of the compounds under investigation.

the imidazole-based dual ETA and ATI receptor antagonists have a similar binding mode to the ETA receptor and AT1 receptor, and the binding modes of the imidazoles in the active site are similar to those of the nonimidazole-based ETA and AT1 antagonists, and the imidazole group is not the key binding group in the active site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis and pharmacological evaluation of a series of imidazole compounds as dual AT 1 and ETA receptor inhibitors.
the molecular modeling of imidazole compounds as dual AT
the design, discovery and optimization of new dual AT1R and ETAR antagonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular modeling approach combining quantum polarized ligands docking, MM/GBSA and 3DQSAR analysis is a powerful tool to evaluate and design dual AT1 and ETa receptor antagonists.

the imidazole ring, the trimethylpyrroline ring and the cyclooctyl ring are important for the activity of dual AT1 and ETa receptor antagonists, while the cyclohexyl and the methoxymethyl groups are important for the antagonism of AT1 receptor and the cyclohexanone and the cyclopentanone groups are important for that of ETA receptor.
the molecular docking study is very important for the drug designing process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the imidazole derivatives could be a promising lead compound for further development as a dual ETA and ATI receptor antagonist.
the imidazole derivatives are a good starting point to develop dual ETA and ATI receptor antagonists.
QPLD, MM/GBSA and pharmacophore based virtual screening are useful tools for drug design and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual antagonists are likely to have a different binding mode from the single antagonists.
the combination of QPLD with MM/GBSA and 3D QSAR analysis is a very useful approach to the rational design of novel potent dual antagonists.
a dual AT1R and ETAR antagonist may be a better antihypertension agent than the single antagonists.
